title: The 8 Best Bandsaw Blades for Woodworking 2026
h1: The 8 Best Bandsaw Blades for Woodworking 2026
metaDescription: Our 8 picks for bandsaw blades for woodworking 2026, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at bandsaw blades for woodworking 2026 using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: Olson Saw FB19293DB Bandsaw Blade 3/8-Inch x 93-1/2-Inch, 4 TPI
products.blurb: Key specs: 3/8-inch width, 4 TPI general-purpose geometry, Thin-kerf, flex-back high-carbon steel, Skip-tooth style with raker set pattern.
strengths: 4 TPI balances resaw speed and curve-cutting ability in a single blade
3/8-inch width tracks straight cuts while still handling tighter curves
Flex-back design reduces wear on wheels, tires, and bearings
Olson is a reference brand woodworkers reach for first when upgrading from stock blades
limitations: High-carbon steel is not as long-lived as bi-metal in abrasive hardwoods
Fixed length -- confirm your bandsaw's blade length before ordering
features: Skip-tooth style with raker set pattern
products.bestFor: buyers who want the best overall package

products.name: Starrett BM1014 Bi-Metal Band Saw Blade, 1/2-Inch Width, 10-14 TPI
products.blurb: Key specs: 1/2-inch width, variable 10-14 TPI, Bi-metal construction with hardened teeth, .020-inch thin-kerf body.
strengths: Starrett's quality control produces consistent, precisely-set teeth
Variable 10-14 TPI reduces vibration and harmonics compared to single-pitch blades
Bi-metal teeth hold an edge far longer than carbon steel
Starrett is a precision measurement and blade manufacturer trusted across metal and wood shops
limitations: Marketed primarily as a portable band saw blade -- check width and length against your stationary saw's wheels
Fine 10-14 TPI is slower than a 4-6 TPI blade for thick resaw cuts

products.name: Olson Saw BM82864BL Bi-Metal Band Saw Blade, 1/2-Inch x 64-1/2-Inch, 18 TPI
products.blurb: Key specs: Bi-metal construction with hardened teeth, 18 TPI regular tooth, raker set, 1/2-inch width, 64-1/2-inch length.
strengths: Bi-metal construction doubles or triples blade life compared to carbon steel in hardwood
Hardened teeth maintain sharpness through dense hardwoods and abrasive material
Flexible backing handles repeated wheel flex without fatigue fractures
Olson is one of the most widely available bi-metal bandsaw blade brands in US woodworking supply
limitations: More expensive per blade than carbon steel
64-1/2-inch length fits smaller benchtop saws -- verify length for larger 14-inch saws

products.name: Laguna Resaw King Carbide-Tip Bandsaw Blade, 3/4-Inch x 115-Inch, Vari-Tooth
products.blurb: Key specs: C4 carbide teeth, individually brazed, Vari-tooth 12-14-16mm pitch reduces vibration, 3/4-inch width, 115-inch length.
strengths: Carbide teeth last far longer than carbon steel or bi-metal in equivalent use
Vari-tooth pitch minimizes harmonics for ultra-smooth, wafer-thin veneer cuts
Stays sharp through abrasive exotic hardwoods that quickly dull carbon blades
Can be resharpened multiple times, extending the investment
limitations: Very high price -- significant upfront investment
Requires professional carbide sharpening when it eventually dulls
features: Made in Germany, finish-ground in the USA

products.name: POWERTEC 67-1/2-Inch Bandsaw Blade, 1/8-Inch x 14 TPI
products.blurb: Key specs: 1/8-inch width for curve cutting, 14 TPI for fine finish, Carbon steel construction.
strengths: 14 TPI produces a smooth cut surface that needs minimal sanding
1/8-inch width handles moderate-to-tight curves in furniture parts
Affordable enough to keep a dedicated curve-cutting blade on hand
Widely stocked, easy replacement blade
limitations: 14 TPI cuts slowly -- not for resawing or fast rough work
Sized for 10-inch benchtop saws -- confirm length matches your bandsaw
features: Sized for 10-inch benchtop bandsaws such as the Rikon 10-300

products.name: POWERTEC 80-Inch Bandsaw Blade, 1/8-Inch x 14 TPI
products.blurb: Key specs: 1/8-inch width for tight radius cuts, 14 TPI, 80-inch length, sized for 12-inch bandsaws such as Craftsman.
strengths: 1/8-inch width cuts a tighter radius than 1/4-inch or 3/8-inch blades
Essential for bandsaw boxes, vessel cutting, and organic shapes
14 TPI produces a smooth cut surface in thin stock
Low cost keeps a narrow blade on hand without a big investment
limitations: Narrow blades deflect more easily in thick hardwood -- keep cuts shallow
Requires careful tracking adjustment -- narrow blades are more sensitive to wheel setup
features: 80-inch length, sized for 12-inch bandsaws such as Craftsman

products.name: POWERTEC 105-Inch Bandsaw Blade, 1/2-Inch x 3 TPI
products.blurb: Key specs: 1/2-inch width, 3 TPI, Carbon steel, 105-inch length for 14-inch bandsaws with riser blocks.
strengths: Lowest price in the woodworking bandsaw blade category
1/2-inch, 3 TPI works for both moderate curves and light resawing
Good for learning bandsaw tension, tracking, and drift compensation
Fits 14-inch saws upgraded with a riser block
limitations: Carbon steel -- shorter life than bi-metal or carbide alternatives
Quality control less consistent than Starrett, Olson, or Timber Wolf
features: 105-inch length for 14-inch bandsaws with riser blocks
products.bestFor: value-focused buyers who want the most for their money

products.name: Lenox Diemaster 2 Bi-Metal Band Saw Blade, 93.5-Inch x 1/2-Inch, 14 TPI
products.blurb: Key specs: Bi-metal construction, hook tooth, Raker set, positive rake, 14 TPI, Works in wood and soft metals.
strengths: Hook tooth geometry with positive rake cuts aggressively while staying smooth
Bi-metal extends life significantly over carbon steel in both wood and metal cutting
Lenox manufactures blades with consistent quality control
Works in both wood and soft metals -- adds shop versatility
limitations: Not optimized specifically for wood resawing -- a dedicated Timber Wolf or Laguna blade is better for that task
Higher cost than single-material wood blades
features: Works in wood and soft metals

howWeChose: Picks are based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. We don't claim our own testing.
We do not list prices or star ratings because they change. Check Amazon for current details.
